name: Go
body: HSTS is preloaded, framing is limited with frame-ancestors, and Core Web Vitals pass for real visitors. But go.dev has Google MX records and no SPF or DMARC record, so anyone can send mail in its name.
lesson: Publish SPF for the senders you use and a DMARC policy. Start at p=none with reports, then tighten.
summary: go.dev scores 81 out of 100 (B). 0 checks fail now, 23 are at risk, and 14 pass. Fix first: 290 images have no alt attribute.

fix.title: 290 images have no alt attribute
fix.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

fix.title: 17 pages have no meta description
fix.evidence: /solutions/case-studies, /solutions/use-cases, /doc/security/, /learn/ and 13 more. Google and AI answers then write their own snippet from whatever text they find.
fix.fix: Write a 50 to 160 character description for each page that says what a reader gets.

fix.title: X-Content-Type-Options is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers may guess a file's type and run it as script. Missing on all 18 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 18 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 18 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
fix.evidence: Google Tag Manager appears in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
fix.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

works.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
HSTS is sent with a long max-age
The start page declares its language
The start page arrived in 753 ms
Share cards have a title, description, image, and URL
